method: Independent static reading of the supplied complete ASM and pseudocode; no native call, process access, build or product change. No additional coverage claims are created by this review.
status: Requested actor-AI core distinctions independently confirmed; no implementation or universal freeze claim.
scope: Selected initialization, normal actor dispatch, motion-clock, direct VM-update, native stop-ID1 and stop-slot insertion bodies.
conclusions: 3BFD30 checks Actor+2488 bit0x80 before descriptor vtable+8.3DB430 ->4117D0 ->3DACB0 ->3B44D0 is a concrete preparation path;3B44D0 creates/stores the BDX VM at Actor+1456, starts event1, copies pose state and sets bit0x80. Normal one-time initialization is supported, not an unconditional per-frame AI callback.

The normal dispatcher passes Actor+344 and float frame delta in XMM1 to3C6740. That body multiplies by motion+336 and advances motion frames/transitions.3B4420/3B4460 instead fetch the QWORD Actor+1456 for YSVM_UpdateTree. These data paths are distinct.
3D9130 passes ID1 to3DBAA0;3DBAA0 supplies duration0.0 in XMM2 to3B6730 for its native filtered actor set.3D9130 later calls3B42D0 with ID1. Thus ID1 cannot be assumed trainer-private.

3BFD30 performs descriptor+64/+72 and initialization before the stop gate. Its stopped path may still call3C73C0 and publish the actor to a postprocessing list.3B4460 has no local stop predicate. Animation freezing or a stop entry does not prove that every synchronous/event AI path is paused.

40A920 chooses a matching stop slot or the last empty one among four. If all four contain different nonzero IDs, R9 remainsnull and the store at40A966 targets null+4. The aggregate rebuild also trusts the stop-table lookup result. Future callers need capacity/table checks and ownership beyond ID equality.
remaining: The other report claims and all enemy/boss/synchronous VM callers were not independently exhausted in this scoped review.
